metadata.title: Autonomy Breaks at the Control Layer
metadata.description:
The expensive failure is not model intelligence. It is the control layer that collapses before autonomy becomes profitable.

Claim: Autonomy fails economically when action costs, oversight, and integration controls rise faster than capability.

Evidence: The latest dashboard shows 2361 thumbnail impressions, 0.59 percent CTR, and 40.05 percent average viewed.; The local upload report frames the three-tax argument around control failure before autonomy.; The package has Shorts and related-video follow-through already pointing to this cinematic.

Technical dilemma: Where does autonomy become expensive: the model, the action surface, or the control layer around it?

Author note: The video has enough retention to justify a cleaner title; the weak signal is packaging, not obvious rejection.

Source: https://lambpetros.substack.com/p/the-autonomy-tax

Research breakdown: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1laAYOsrTLg

before.title: The AI Autonomy Tax | A Cinematic Research Brief
before.description:
The expensive failure in enterprise AI is not model intelligence. It is the control layer that collapses before autonomy ever becomes profitable.

This cinematic brief compresses the three-tax argument into one acquisition path for operators and executives: autonomy costs rise faster than the workflow controls needed to keep those systems safe, accountable, and economically sane.

The companion should drive viewers to the full longform only after landing the causal engine cleanly enough to feel urgent and repeatable.

before.description:
The risk in agent systems is not just the model. It is the architecture you wrapped around it and all the boundaries it quietly opened.

It should attract viewers who need a more operational model of agent safety than red-team spectacle alone.
